surfaces.source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings; path literal read from the pinned 2.1.251 artifact
surfaces.note: The `plugin` kind was routed here too, and is withdrawn. `enabledPlugins` and `extraKnownMarketplaces` are keys in this file, so a plugin does reach Claude Code through it -- but this provider has no merge semantics: `write_bundle_files` calls `remove_managed` and then writes a bundle's bytes verbatim. A `plugin` component carrying `settings.json` would replace the whole file and, because the removal runs first, delete `CLAUDE.md`, `skills`, `agents`, `commands` and `rules` on the way in. It was the only kind across all seven routed to a file rather than a directory, which is the shape that should have prompted the question. Declaring it again means building settings-merge first. Confirmed 2026-08-29 from the pinned 2.1.251 artifact, whose bytes match this baseline's own sha256: the product carries `.claude/settings.json` as a literal, 89 time(s), joined to the home its `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` resolves. The vendor page beside it says the same thing; what the artifact adds is that a wrong path here would now be visible to something rather than to nobody.

surfaces.source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills; path literal read from the pinned 2.1.251 artifact
surfaces.note: Two neighbouring products read this directory, measured from their own pinned bytes. Grok's embedded reference: `skills = true  # scan ~/.claude/skills/ and <cwd>/.claude/skills/`, User tier, Lowest priority, configurable. OpenCode carries `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` as a path literal and the vendor lists it as *Global Claude-compatible*. This provider's ownership is unchanged -- it is Claude Code's own home and this is the harness this provider configures -- but a namespace is removed whole, so a remove here also changes what Grok and OpenCode see. `remove` says the namespaces go whole; it cannot say who else was reading them. Confirmed 2026-08-29 from the pinned 2.1.251 artifact, whose bytes match this baseline's own sha256: the product carries `.claude/skills` as a literal, 51 time(s), joined to the home its `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` resolves. The vendor page beside it says the same thing; what the artifact adds is that a wrong path here would now be visible to something rather than to nobody.

surfaces.note: "Personal rules in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to every project on your machine." Markdown files, optionally with a `paths` frontmatter list that scopes a rule to matching files. Owned so a setup can carry one; no component kind routes here, because `instruction` already routes to CLAUDE.md and one kind with two surfaces would leave a compiler to choose with nothing telling it how Confirmed 2026-08-29 from the pinned 2.1.251 artifact, whose bytes match this baseline's own sha256: the product carries `.claude/rules` as a literal, 9 time(s), joined to the home its `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` resolves. The vendor page beside it says the same thing; what the artifact adds is that a wrong path here would now be visible to something rather than to nobody.

Personal workflow scripts. The vendor: a script saved to `~/.claude/workflows/` is *just for you*, in contrast to a `.claude/workflows/` shared in a repository, and it *runs as a `/<name>` command*. The binary carries `.claude/workflows/` without a `~`, which is why the root took a page to settle -- the audit had called it global on the strength of the literal alone and was corrected before anything was built on it.

Owned from 2026-08-28 so a backup captures it. **Routing no kind**, for the reason grok's `rules` row gives: `command` already routes to the owned `commands`, and one kind on two surfaces makes a consumer's route ambiguous -- the surfaces guard refuses it by name. Both are real, both are user-level, and which a `command` component should reach waits on the per-kind route the consumer is building.

declined.reason: Claude Code stores MCP servers in `.claude.json` -- user scope at the top level, local scope under projects[<path>].mcpServers -- and project scope in a .mcp.json at the project root. There is no .mcp.json under this home. `.claude.json` is in never_touch, so no MCP surface is ownable inside this target and the kind is not declared.

Hooks are configured under a "hooks" key in settings.json. ~/.claude/hooks/ is a convention for the scripts a hook command points at, not a directory Claude Code reads. It is declared the day a setup here ships hook scripts and not before.

Claude Code owns plugins/known_marketplaces.json, plugins/marketplaces, plugins/cache and plugins/data. Held in never_touch: a plugin component projects through settings.json, which this provider does own.

Observed, not documented: with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointing at a target, the product writes this file *inside* that home rather than beside it -- measured 2026-08-28 by installing Claude Code through this provider's own software lifecycle and running `mcp add --scope user` through `launch`. It carries user-scope MCP servers, account state and project history, which the product rewrites on its own schedule. Disclaimed rather than owned: owning it would promise a rollback of an account record.

declined.reason:
Not a path in the target, and named without an extension for that reason: `managed-settings.json` lives at a **system** path, one per operating system, and every recorded path here is relative to the target.

  * Linux — `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json`
  * macOS — `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json`
  * Windows — `%ProgramData%\\ClaudeCode\\managed-settings.json`

All three are path literals in the pinned product. Grok's own compatibility documentation describes the file, and the description is the reason this row exists: *"a protected policy file for allowlists and defaults. Its values take precedence over user, project and local config **and cannot be overridden**."*

**It bears on the `full-auto` posture.** That setup writes `permissions.defaultMode = bypassPermissions` and `sandbox.enabled = false` into the owned `settings.json`. Under a managed policy those keys are correct, at a correct path, in a file the product reads — and a higher layer overrides them. The setup installs, verifies and restores cleanly and **changes nothing**.

That is the third instance of one defect class in this estate: opencode's bare-string `permission`, antigravity's `toolPermissions`, and now a correct key under a layer that outranks it. The first two were fixed by writing the right key; this one cannot be fixed by writing anything, which is why it is written down instead.

**Nothing to own and nothing to check at runtime.** A provider that read a system policy in order to warn about it would be reading a file it promises not to touch, on a path outside every target it is given.
declined.source: path literals measured in the pinned product, 2026-08-28; the precedence sentence is from grok 1.0.5's embedded compatibility reference

configuration_format.note: Strict JSON. Comment support is an open feature request against the vendor (`anthropics/claude-code` #12688, #17968, #29370) and is not implemented, so a `//` in this file is a parse error rather than a stylistic choice. The schema is SchemaStore's rather than the vendor's own, and `tools/validate_setup_schemas.py` fetches and checks against it.
